sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. The article covers only the vowel inventory (10 short / 7 long oral vowels), [expanded]-harmony and vowel merger; tone marks appear on the cited forms but neither tone nor stress/accent is mentioned anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence returns no hits).

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Benard Abraham, Fittokka Gobak & Longdi Sylvanus. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Deko-Dusanga [uya], Iyongiyong [bbs], and Robambami [ibm] Languages in Cross River State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-022. Dallas: SIL International. 64 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sociolinguistic survey plus a 222-item wordlist; Appendix E (printed p. 44 / p. 52) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Section 4.3 'Robambami' (printed p. 6 / p. 14) lists as prior linguistic work only the 1976 Ibadan student papers ('There is no reference to where the articles can be found'), Yul-Ifode 2003 on vowels, Dimmendaal 1978 and Blench's wordlists. sil.org is could not be reached by automated download; the PDF was pulled archived copy (Internet Archive, 8 S…

sources.citation: Yul-Ifode, Shirley O. 2003. The basics of Agoi vowels. In O.-M. Ndimele (ed.), Four decades in the study of Nigerian languages and linguistics: A Festschrift for Kay Williamson, 593-604. Aba: NINLAN (reissue 2019, M & J Grand Orbit).
sources.note: Second published phonology paper on Agoi by the same author; vowels only by title, but may carry an introductory note on tone/stress. Google Books partial view (id qSaRDwAAQBAJ) could be checked from a browser.
